utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated for the moment, please. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please stand up. I think you need to use the other microphone because -- there is facial distortion, voice distortion?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. So you're going to read the solemn declaration that the usher is going to give you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you comfortable, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're going to look at this piece of paper and tell us, yes or no, is your name written on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's see. Don't tell us your name, please. One moment. And now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So finally. It is only a mere formality, but we have to do it. So you're now going to answer questions by Mr. Harmon is going to put to you, please. You have the floor, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to be referring to you as Witness BB. Good afternoon, Witness BB.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell us your nationality, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I'm of Bosniak nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what is your religious faith?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Islam is my faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell us your educational background starting, please, first with your secondary school education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: My education was actually an occupation of the technician for telecommunications, and I graduated from the corresponding secondary school for such a profile.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, the nature of the coursework. What was it exactly that you studied, and in particular, could you tell us what you studied in respect of radios and radio communications, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: In connection with radio communications, I had a subject called "Radio and Radio-Relay Devices"; then there was another subject or course called "Multiplex Systems"; then a course in telegraphy; and subjects in which you study the work of telephone exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you graduate in 1984 with a degree in electronic telecommunications?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you go on to university?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you study two years at university the subject matter of electrotechnics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did any of your service in the JNA in 1984 and 1985 have to do with telecommunications, or was it unrelated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I did something that was unrelated to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Witness BB, could you tell us about your private interest in radios? Did you have such an interest, and how did you pursue that interest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I developed an interest in radio early on, in elementary school, and that is why I decided to enrol in a telecommunications secondary school. Continuously I was engaged as an amateur in electronics, repairing radio and TV sets or any other electronic devices, or assembling them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, did you maintain that interest in radios up to the time of the commencement of the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's focus our attention on the war in Bosnia and let me ask you, in October of 1992, did you join an anti-electronic warfare unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you remain in that unit until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, while you were engaged in that kind of activity, were you stationed at various locations in eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you identify by name those locations, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I can. Konjuh, Okresanica, the 2nd Corps command, Par Selo, and some other locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have Prosecutor's Exhibit 138 placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: While that's being placed on the ELMO, Witness BB, can you tell us the time periods when you were stationed at Okresanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I was at Okresanica on several occasions. For the last time I arrived in May 1995, and I stayed until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, to your left, Witness BB, is a map. Could you just point out, please, the locations where you were stationed, starting with Okresanica, please, and then point to the location of Konjuh where you were also stationed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: This is Okresanica; this is Konjuh.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has pointed first to the green dot on the left-hand side of Prosecutor's Exhibit 138 with the word "Okresanica" next to it, and he next pointed to the green dot below it that has "Konjuh" written alongside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, when you were at Okresanica and Konjuh, whose communications were you intercepting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I was intercepting the communications of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's narrow down the focus of this examination a little more. You said you were at Okresanica from May 1995 onward, and I'd like to focus on that period of time, particularly the period of time in July of 1995. First of all, what were your duties during that time period at Okresanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I had two duties; first I worked as an operator and after that I switched to work as an operator on encryption, as a signalsman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As an operator, briefly what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: We monitored certain frequencies coming from certain directions. When we would identify a conversation on that frequency, we would switch on the recording of that conversation, and after that, when the conversation ended, we would rewind the conversation, listen to it, take it down in a notebook and hand it over to the signalsman operator.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say you'd hand it over to the signalsman operator, that was the individual who would type the entry in the notebook onto a monitor, encrypt it and forward it on to the higher command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let's focus on your role as the person who would encrypt these messages from the notebooks and forward them on to your higher command, because that's the position you also held, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As I understand the procedure, and as the Judges have heard from other witnesses, a notebook would be given to the person whose obligation it was to type exactly the contents from the notebook onto the monitor. Is that specifically what the obligation was and what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As an individual who did this encryption and typing work, was there ever an occasion when you had to relisten to a tape, or you requested that the intercept operator who had presented you with the notebook relisten to the tape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When did that happen and under what circumstances did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: If I would note any irregularities in the text I received, anything that was not logical, I would ask the operator who transcribed it to explain it to me, and what would most often happen would be that the tape would be relistened to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And who would relisten to the tape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The operator who originally took it down or another operator, but most frequently several persons. Sometimes I was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if there were changes that were made or heard on a relistening, how would those be communicated to you as the person who had to forward the message on to the higher command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I would enter the changes into the monitor. I would type in those changes which had been identified and then encode it and send it to the higher command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would the changes then be noted back in the notebook that may have had something that needed to be changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: If only a name was involved, a very short and clear piece of information, in most cases this was not changed in the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you, again focusing on your position as the person who encrypted and transmitted these messages, when you received a notebook, Witness BB, from an intercept operator, it was customary, was it not, for the intercept operator, at the end of the transmission that had been copied into the notebook, to sign his initials or name? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: In some cases the operator would sign, but there were cases when this was left out by omission.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: While you were the person who was doing the encrypting, was it customary for you or the other person who was encrypting, after the message had been transmitted, to sign either your name or your initials in the notebook in respect of the particular conversation that had been transmitted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes. I would place my signature in the notebook for the conversations that had been forwarded to the higher command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, with the assistance of the usher, if I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 283 placed in front of the witness, and that is found at tab 5. Mr. Usher, if you could turn that -- if you could turn to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If you could turn to page 00804765.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, if you look at the bottom of page 765, you will see two initials and a name. I do not want to identify orally the name or the two initials, but am I correct, in referring to this particular handwritten notation in this notebook, that the two initials are the initials of the intercept operator? Am I correct on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And am I correct that the name that appears under that is your name, reflecting the fact that you were the individual who typed this into the computer, encrypted this message, and sent it on to your forward command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Usher, if you could kindly turn to the last three digits in this same exhibit, 803.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Witness BB, is there a name at the bottom of that particular intercept, bottom of page 803?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does that name represent the name of the individual who transmitted this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes. That is the name of the person who typed out, encrypted, and forwarded this conversation to the higher command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, do you know, Witness BB, if this procedure was the procedure that was followed all the time at Okresanica or was this introduced later in time? You testified earlier that you had been there on more than one occasion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The last period of time that I spent there was a period when this procedure was respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, I'm going to ask you now about a specific number of intercepted communications, and let me ask you first, did you have an opportunity to review various notebooks, copies of those notebooks, in my office before coming to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did I ask you to attempt to identify certain conversations as being the conversations that you personally intercepted and ask you to date those conversations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn, first of all, if I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If the witness could have placed in front of him a series of exhibits. We'll start with Prosecutor's Exhibit 340.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, could you take a look at -- we won't put that on the ELMO. If you would just take a look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 340.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Usher, if you would kindly also open the binder to tab 7, Prosecutor's Exhibit 285, and if you could turn to page 00800787.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, do you recognise in Prosecutor's Exhibit 340 your own handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is this a communication that you personally intercepted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the corresponding notebook on page 787. Is Prosecutor's Exhibit 340 identical to the intercepted communication that is found on page 787, the bottom left-hand side of 787?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes, it is identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did I ask you, Witness, to attempt to date this particular conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me refer you to the notebook, Prosecutor's Exhibit 285.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you would turn to page -- the last three digits in the ERN number are 781.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see a date in the upper left-hand corner on page 781?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, your conversation is then found at page 787.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you turn to page 800, the last three digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness, referring to page 800 of Prosecutor's Exhibit 285, do you see a date on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know who wrote that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I wrote that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your conversation appears somewhere between the date of the 12th and this date of the 13th. Are you therefore able to conclude when this particular conversation found in Prosecutor's 340 was intercepted and recorded in the notebook?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes. The 12th of the July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will now read this particular intercept into the record, starting with:

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: "785.000, Ch 5, 1156 hrs (Duty Officer at the Badem OC/Operation Centre/) X - Y (Zlatar /code-name/) (Barely audible)" Now, let me stop the reading here and just ask you a question, Witness BB. Is the letter "Y," then, that's referenced in the remaining part of the text Zlatar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is "X" then Badem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know "Badem" and "Zlatar" to be code names for particular military units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will now continue my reading. "Y: Do you have ... regarding the link up with your neighbour on the right. X: Nothing has changed. It's all the same as it used to be. Y: ... they are moving towards Konjevic Polje and (Kosat?) X: We have information. It's exactly like that. Y: What action did you take, for God sake? X: Listen, General Krstic is here ... ... I ... Duty Officer ... to order. Y: ... X: It's been /?useless/ for three years and no one cared. Let me please put you through to General Krstic. He's up there in his office. Hello! (Line disconnected)" Now, we've concluded with this particular exhibit, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 341 placed in front of the witness. Mr. Usher, if you would kindly take Prosecutor's Exhibit 283, the binder; 283 is found at tab 5, and if you could open Prosecutor's Exhibit 283 to page 826 of the ERN number, the last three digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, would you compare Prosecutor's Exhibit 341, which is an extract from the notebook, 283, and compare it with the entry that is found on page -- the last three digits being 826. Is the extract and the conversation that's found in Prosecutor's 825 identical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, is the handwriting that's found in Prosecutor's Exhibit 341 your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were the person who intercepted this information that's reflected in this entry in the notebook?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this question: Did you also attempt to date this conversation for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Usher, if you would kindly turn this -- in Prosecutor's Exhibit 283, if you go back to page 826. I apologise, Mr. Usher. 755. If you would go back to page 755.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see a date on page 755 in this notebook?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The 2nd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Usher, if you would go past the conversation and turn to page 836.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see a date on 836 in Prosecutor's Exhibit 283?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in whose handwriting is that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: That's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did I ask you last night, Witness, to analyse this notebook by comparing the times and attempting to date this specific conversation, and were you able to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Based on your analysis, what was the date that you concluded you intercepted this particular conversation, the conversation that's found on Prosecutor's Exhibit 341?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me now read this very brief entry into the record. I'm reading from Prosecutor's Exhibit 341: "785.000, Ch 1, 1210 hours. Krstic - Krsmanovic. Krstic wants the buses to start moving right away." Witness BB, is this a transcript of the conversation or is this a summary of what was heard? Can you explain this particular intercepted communication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: This is the summary of the conversation that was heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And why wasn't there a verbatim entry in this particular conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you occasionally summarise an entry in notebooks when you had intercepted something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How was it that you were able to identify the speakers Krstic and Krsmanovic in respect of Prosecutor's Exhibit 341?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: By listening to the recording in which they introduced themselves. So I was able to determine who the participants in the conversation were. However, probably this piece of information that has been recorded here, that is to say, the summary, is the only thing that sounded like some kind of information, and so on the basis of that, I wrote down this in summary form and did not transcribe the entire conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, we'll turn to the next exhibit. It's Prosecutor's Exhibit 342.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That can be shown to the witness, and, Mr. Usher, if you would kindly turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 285, which is found at tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention to page 790 in Prosecutor's Exhibit 285. Witness, can you please compare Prosecutor's Exhibit 342 with the notebook entry that is found at page 790 in Prosecutor's 285, and tell the Judges whether these are identical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is this your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did I ask you to attempt to date to conversation as well, Witness BB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you would kindly turn to page 781 in Prosecutor's Exhibit 285.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, you've testified previously about this. Is there a date in the upper left-hand corner of 781?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that date July the 12th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And that is written in your hand, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Let me turn your attention now to page 800 in this particular notebook. Do you see a date in the right-hand, lower portion of that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the date that you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness BB, the conversation that's the object of Prosecutor's Exhibit 342 appears to be between the dates of July the 12th and July the 13th notations that are in the notebook. What is the date you, therefore, conclude you intercepted this particular conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: The 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will read this particular conversation into the record. "785.000, Channel 5. Participants: X (can't be heard) - Krsmanovic. K: Is Djukic there? X: ... K: If he can let him send me these trailer-trucks immediately. X: ... K: Good. All right. X: ... K: Here at my place in the command. (Poor audibility)" Let me ask you, in this exhibit and in previous exhibits, Witness BB, there appear to be dots at various locations within the text of the conversation. What is represented by those dots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: They mean part of the conversation which was completely incomprehensible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next exhibit, please, Mr. Usher, it's Prosecutor's Exhibit 343, and Mr. Usher, if you would kindly turn to the corresponding page in Prosecutor's Exhibit 285, again found at tab 7, if you would turn to page 791.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, comparing the exhibit, Prosecutor's Exhibit 343 with the entry that's found in Prosecutor's Exhibit 285, at pages 791 and 792, are they identical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you intercepted this particular communication; is that correct, Witness BB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, I asked you to attempt to date this conversation, and let's go through that exercise very quickly again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you would turn to 781 in Prosecutor's Exhibit 285.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a date we've seen before. The date of July the 12th, 1995 appears on the upper left-hand corner at page 781; is that correct, Witness BB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 800 in this same exhibit, we can see again a date we've seen before, July the 13th, 1995, found on page 800; is that correct, Witness BB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Since the conversation that is reflected in Prosecutor's Exhibit 343 is found between the dates of 12 July 1995 and 13 July 1995, are you able to provide the Trial Chamber with a date when this particular conversation was intercepted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BB
utterances.text: Yes. This conversation was intercepted on the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then I will read this into the record, this conversation. "785.000, Channel 5, 1240 hrs (inaudible) (PANORAMA) X - Y (barely audible). ... Y: We are starting the evacuation of those who want to go to Kladanj. X: OK. Y: Pass it on ... just /let them/ provide transportation. X: ... Y: And reinforce ... with trucks and buses, and a water tank should be sent, to give them water and food. This morning we organised it here, we'll give them everything. I talked with them and we'll accept all of the civilians who want to and they can stay. Those who don't want to can choose where they'll go. X: ... Y: ... see you, bye. /signed/" with a name inserted therein. Let me turn to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we're rapidly coming to a close for the day's work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Mr. Harmon. I think that we should break for the weekend and resume next Monday at 9.30 with this witness. Is that right? Perhaps it would be better to finish with this witness and then go on, but we'll see. Witness, we are going to continue after the weekend. I hope that you have a good weekend here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
